segments: The seventeenth dynasty.
The Arab kings.
... {OCR?} musk bags,
and chief garments,
and much saffron,
and other produce.
And he was received with honor,
and two thousand captive men were given to him,
and among them were twenty women and ten children.
For this Nasr said:
"During all the time that I was in Constantinople, I did not see the king speak when he heard my words through the interpreters,
but only with his head he would say:
'Yes.'
And his maternal uncle used to speak on his behalf,
because he was still a child."
And when many of the Arabs had been baptized,
the king of the Romans commanded:
"Let all of them go as far as the border between us and the Arabs,
and he who desires Christianity,
and turns back from there and comes,
we will receive him as a true believer."
Nasr said
that two artisans {OCR?}, drowning craftsmen {OCR?} from the people of Africa, and many others, turned back from the border,
and did not wish to come with us.
And in the year
(1177 of the Greeks,
866 {OCR?} of our Lord?), which is the year 247
247 of the Arabs,
al-Muntasir, the son of al-Mutawakkil, hatched a plot with the Turkish slaves,
and they went in against his father with swords while he was drunk,
al-Muntasir {OCR?} his son six months.
this one, when and they killed him {OCR?}.
After al-Mutawakkil reigned,
he coerced {OCR?}
both his brothers, al-Mu'tazz and al-Mu'ayyad, while threatening them with death,
if they did not renounce their right to the kingdom,
and commit it to him and to his sons,
contrary to what al-Mutawakkil their father had determined,
namely, that each one of them should reign after his fellow.
And when they were coerced,
they wrote with their own handwriting,
and had righteous men bear witness against themselves,
that of their own good will they had renounced their right,
and that al-Muntasir their brother had authority to make his son king after him.
And thus, when the murder of his father did not suffice him,
he even acted deceitfully against his brothers.
He lived for only six months,
and died of the pain of quinsy when he was twenty-five years old.
And it is said
that before he died he saw in a dream as if he were ascending a ladder,
and when he reached twenty-five rungs, it was said to him:
"Stop,
this is your end."
After al-Mu[sta'in reigned] {OCR?} three years and three months.
